## MechWarrior 1 Remake 1.1.0

Things to spend your money on, a new soundtrack, a way out when you're stranded, and a graded ending.

- **Permanent upgrades:** the Mech Complex has a new SUPPLY screen, and its upgrades are yours for good.
  - **Heat sinks and armour:** each kit is one extra heat sink or one extra point of armour beyond the usual limit. They weigh nothing and can't be critically hit.
  - **Where kits go:** the company owns its kits. With ASSIGN you put any number on any of your 'Mechs, yours or your lancemates', and move them later. When a 'Mech is sold or lost, its kits go back to your stores.
  - **Weapon steps:** each power step adds 5% to a weapon type's damage, and each range step adds 10 m to its range, with the heat unchanged. A step applies to every weapon of that type in your company. Range steps can at most double a weapon's own range.
  - **Prices:** upgrades are expensive, and each one costs more than the last: a heat sink starts at 3 million C-bills, an armour point at 500,000 and a weapon step at 5 million. SUPPLY asks before you buy one, because upgrades can't be sold back.
  - **Who gets them:** only your side. An enemy carrying the same weapon gets nothing.
- **An arms dealer:** SUPPLY also lists the dealer's weapons, ammunition and equipment for the world you're on. Bought items go into your stores, ready for the Mech Lab to fit. This is where you find the weapons no enemy ever carries, such as the PPC, the Ultra and LB-X autocannons, Streak SRMs, MASC, ECM and the targeting computer. Clan gear is rare, found only on tier 3 worlds and the Clan worlds. The stock changes when the market does, and the dealer buys items back at the world's going rate, as with 'Mechs.
- **A new soundtrack:** MechWarrior's five songs are back as rock arrangements, each at its original moment:
  - the theme on the title and between missions;
  - the Bar's song when you walk in;
  - a song for a contract won;
  - a lament when a failed mission costs you a lancemate;
  - the ending's song over the credits.

  In battle, six new combat songs play from a shuffle. None plays twice until you've heard all six, and when one ends the next starts. The theme comes back after a mission, and when one of MechWarrior's other songs ends.
- **Never stranded:** if your company is stuck on a world with no contracts it can take, can't afford the trip out and can't sell enough to pay for it, a merchant JumpShip now offers passage. It takes you to the nearest world that will deal with you, free of fare and wages. The trip takes longer than a paid one. The hub tells you when this is on offer, and the STARPORT's GO becomes TAKE PASSAGE. Before you travel to a world you couldn't afford to leave, the starport warns you.
- **No deadline, and a graded ending:** the hunt for the Dark Wing still has no deadline, and now the ending grades how long it took. The clock starts when you first face Grig's men at Land's End and stops when the Dark Wing falls. After the victory, a page gives your grade:
  - Exceptional: within five years, the time the council allowed;
  - Good: within ten years;
  - Late: longer than that.

  The news no longer reports a succession that, with no deadline, never comes. Games saved in an earlier version keep working: if the hunt had already begun, its start is taken from your log.
- **Your saves now live in a BattleTech folder:** there's nothing to do. Your settings and saved games move there by themselves the first time 1.1.0 starts. MechWarrior 1 started on its own also finds Pirate's Moon after the launcher moved its folder.
- **Damaged saves on Windows:** a saved game that can't be read is now set aside as a .bad file, as on the Mac and Linux. Before, it stayed in its slot.
- **Saved games:** 1.1.0 reads saves from every earlier version. Saves written by 1.1.0 can't be loaded by an older version.

You still need your own copies of MechWarrior (1989), MechWarrior 3 and Pirate's Moon.
